requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.references.coverage.report`. The obligations below each map to a test with assertions.

**Obligations and the tests that check them**

1. **`habeas status` warns about every item without recent coverage, naming file, line, kind and name.**
   - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts that status output has a "Coverage warnings" section.
   - It asserts the exact warning line for `render` (`<file>:<line>: function render has no recent coverage`), and that the covered `parse` is not warned about.
   - It then asserts that `parse` is warned about once history is cut by a shallow clone.
   - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` covers the examples `requirements.references.coverage.reauthored` and `requirements.references.coverage.new_function`.
   - It asserts that `helper`, which no record ever read, is warned about at once.
   - It asserts that `parse` is not warned about after two re-authorings, and is warned about after the third.

2. **`habeas author` warns after it finishes.**
   - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_coverage_warnings_on_stderr]` runs the real binary with `author --all`.
   - It asserts "Coverage warnings" and the warning line for `helper` on stderr, and nothing on stdout.
   - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` asserts the warning for `orphan` even when nothing is assessed.
   - It does this for `author`, `author --all`, and `author-evidence`.
   - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics]` and `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]` assert that a finished batch, and the `--stdout` path, report on stderr. The `--stdout` case also confirms that stdout carries only the record.

3. **Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.**
   - Inline `mod tests`: the `fixture` item in `mod tests` is never warned about in `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item`.
   - Out-of-line `tests.rs` and `tests/mod.rs`: `tests/coverage.rs#fn[items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about]` asserts the exact warned set. It excludes `foo_fixture` and `bar_fixture`, while `in_foo` is still warned about.
   - Path classification: `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]` has positive and negative path cases.
   - Interaction with test errors: `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_is_an_error_not_a_coverage_warning]` asserts that a bare `#[test]` is an error, not a warning, and that a plain helper is still warned about. That matches the `requirements.references.coverage.test_module` example.

4. **A warning does not fail validation.** `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` asserts that validation errors do not mention the warned item `parse`. The `author` test asserts exit success while warnings are printed.

5. **Repository validation does not read Git history.** `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` deletes the Git object database. It asserts that `validate_repository` errors are unchanged, while `coverage_warnings` reports incomplete history.

**Remaining observations**

- The `kind` in the warning is asserted as "function" in the report tests.
- Other kinds (struct, enum, union) get their kind names from `item_kind` and are asserted in the `src/rust_coverage.rs` unit tests. That is a mapping with no distinct reporting behavior, so I do not count it as a gap.
- The history-window details belong to `requirements.references.coverage.history`, whose own tests (shallow clone, uncommitted records, the window setting) are present.

No unacknowledged gap found.

text: :::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
:::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
